To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

We have developed a novel class of dual‐purpose probes that can be used for the analysis of nucleic acid conformation and recognition in solution by fluorescence and in solid state by X‐ray diffraction, and we provide a detailed protocol of their synthesis, site‐specific incorporation in DNA and RNA, as well as their use for the analysis of bacterial decoding site (A‐site RNA) and G‐quadraplex structures of the telomeric DNA overhang.

the synthesis of DNA and RNA oligos containing a dual‐purpose selenium‐modified fluorescent nucleoside probe was successfully developed, and these probes were successfully used to investigate the conformation and function of bacterial decoding site and human telomeric DNA structures.

we have developed a novel dual‐purpose fluorescent nucleoside probe, 5‐selenium‐modified uracils, that can serve as a conformationally sensitive fluorophore and an X‐ray phasing agent for crystallographic studies of nucleic acids in solution and in the solid state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing new chemical methods to synthesize and characterize DNA and RNA analogues.
the development of novel nucleosides and nucleotides for the synthesis of DNA and RNA oligomers.

the synthesis of novel selenium‐containing fluorescent nucleoside probes, their site‐specific and site‐unspecified incorporation into DNA and RNA oligomers and the development of efficient tools that will enable direct correlation of oligonucleotide structure and recognition in both solution and solid state at atomic resolutions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is a very interesting article.

we have developed efficient synthetic procedures that allow the synthesis of the phosphoramidite of the dual‐purpose fluorescent nucleoside probes and their subsequent incorporation into DNA and RNA oligomers by automated synthesis.
the 5‐selenium‐modified nucleoside probes developed here are efficient tools to analyze the structure and recognition abilities of DNA and RNA in solution and in the solid phase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 5‐SePhU phosphoramidite can be used to prepare DNA and RNA oligomers with site‐specific incorporation of a dual‐purpose 5‐selenium‐modified nucleotide.

we developed an efficient synthetic protocol for the preparation of DNA and RNA oligomers containing a 5‐S‐modified nucleotide, and that these oligomers were used to probe the conformation and function of RNA and DNA.
the 5‐selenium modified nucleobases are excellent probes for studying RNA and DNA structures by fluorescence and X‐ray crystal structures.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the 5‐selenium‐modified nucleoside probes can be used as a tool for structural studies of DNA and RNA oligomers, and that they can be incorporated into oligonucleotide sequences by automated phosphoramidite chemistry.

the 5‐selenium‐modified nucleosides are versatile probes that can be incorporated into DNA and RNA motifs and can be used as a tool to analyze the structural features and ligand binding properties of nucleic acid structures.
the dual‐purpose 5‐selenium‐modified uracile analogs are efficient tools to study RNA and DNA structures in solution by fluorescence, and in solid state by X‐ray diffraction.
